## Automated Audit & Fix Execution

Execute the full audit workflow from docs/AUDIT_PROMPT.md and write complete findings to docs/REPORT_2.md, then auto-implement fixes.

### Phase 1: Run Full Audit (per docs/AUDIT_PROMPT.md)

1. Read docs/REPORT.md end-to-end — mark each finding status
2. Read docs/INDEX.md, docs/PERMISSION_MATRIX.md, docs/PRD.md, docs/ONBOARDING.md, CLAUDE.md
3. Read .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/SKILL.md
4. Build graph: mcp__code-review-graph__build_or_update_graph_tool(full_rebuild=false)
5. Get minimal context: mcp__code-review_graph__get_minimal_context
6. Pull live schema: mcp__supabase__list_tables(schemas=["public"], verbose=true)
7. Pull security advisors: mcp__supabase__get_advisors(type="security")
8. Pull performance advisors: mcp__supabase__get_advisors(type="performance")
9. Pull API logs: mcp__supabase__get_logs(service="api")
10. Pull edge-function logs: mcp__supabase__get_logs(service="edge-function")
11. Run git log --oneline -20 and git status

### Phase 2: Graph-First Static Analysis

Use code-review-graph tools:
- list_graph_stats
- list_communities + get_architecture_overview
- list_flows (sort by criticality, limit 50)
- find_large_functions(min_lines=50)
- refactor_tool(mode="dead_code")
- get_hub_nodes(top_n=20)
- get_bridge_nodes(top_n=20)
- get_knowledge_gaps
- get_surprising_connections(top_n=15)
- get_impact_radius(base="HEAD~5")
- get_review_context(base="HEAD~5", include_source=true)

### Phase 3: Dimension Audit

Audit all dimensions with evidence:
A. UI/UX — mobile-first 360px, loading/empty/error states, accessibility, toast, dropdown, modal, form, table
B. Database — school_id, RLS, indexes, soft/hard delete, audit columns, migrations, type drift
C. Security — direct supabase.auth calls outside AuthContext, RLS gaps, idempotency, secrets, XSS, SQL injection
D. Code Quality — large functions, dead code, magic strings, any types, console.log, TODO
E. Performance — bundle size, re-renders, queries, realtime leaks
F. Feature Completeness — PRD matrix, edge functions, permissions, i18n
G. Bugs/Errors — log patterns, build/lint/type errors, race conditions
H. Documentation — drift, spec vs code

### Phase 4: Write Complete docs/REPORT_2.md

Structure (mandatory sections in order):
1. Executive Summary — grade (A-F), counts (CRITICAL/HIGH/MED/LOW/INFO), top wins/risks
2. REPORT.md Progress Tracker — table with status + evidence + commit
3. UI/UX Audit — per-page matrix + findings
4. Database Audit — schema, RLS, indexes, type drift, migrations
5. Security Audit — advisor output, RLS gaps, secrets
6. Code Quality — large functions, dead code, magic strings
7. Performance — bundle, re-renders, queries
8. Feature Completeness — PRD matrix, edge functions
9. Bugs/Errors/Failures — log patterns, build/lint/type errors
10. Documentation — drift, missing
11. Best Practices Found — what we do right
12. Worst Practices Found — what we do wrong
13. Threats & Warnings — future risks
14. Future Plan & Direction
15. Priority Action Plan — ranked, effort estimate

Every finding needs: file:line, severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/INFO), confidence (HIGH/MED/LOW), evidence.

### Phase 5: Auto-Implement Fixes

After REPORT_2.md is written, automatically implement fixes for:

CRITICAL severity:
- RLS policy gaps on any table without policies
- Missing idempotency keys in edge functions
- Direct supabase.auth calls outside AuthContext
- Security vulnerabilities from advisor reports

HIGH severity:
- Type drift — run supabase gen types typescript and update types.ts
- Dead code removal
- Missing indexes on foreign keys
- Loading/empty/error states in UI components

MEDIUM severity:
- Large functions (>50 lines) — refactor to smaller units
- Any types — add proper typing
- console.log/debugger removal

For each fix: make the code change, write concise commit, create migration if needed.

### Completion

Report:
- Sections completed count
- Bugs fixed count by severity
- Migrations created (if any)
- Time spent
